Subject: SLO probe & GPU fit: streaming workload shape + pilot plan

Hi Eliza / Auratek team — thanks again for the deep dive earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on a short technical pilot for Dedicated capacity: 

Call highlights
- Target latency: 75 ms p95 for interactive streaming responses at 512-token average output (end-to-end).
- Expected concurrency: bursty peaks up to 80 concurrent streams; steady-state ~30–40.
- Throughput shape: many short requests (50–150 tokens), some long tail up to 1k tokens; streaming chunk size target 64 tokens.
- Quality constraint: no quantization-caused hallucination; prefer 8-bit quant if it meets latency/accuracy.

Proposed validation steps (pilot scope)
1) Workload probe (3 days): run replay of 5k representative requests you provided (attached JSONL) against small Dedicated pool with controlled concurrency to capture token distribution, latency distribution, and KV cache hit rates.
2) Micro-benchmarks (2 days): perf runs on H100-small (3x), A100-80GB (3x), and L4-160GB-equivalent (if available) to show p50/p95/p99 under streaming + fixed concurrency windows.
3) Reserved throughput sizing: use probe data to recommend a reserved slab, and validate at target 80 concurrent streams with our streaming runtime.
4) Observability hooks: add token-level latency traces, per-request model variant, and prefix-KV cache metrics so we can iterate on batching/prefetch rules.

Deliverables and timeline
- Week 0 (start when you say go): workload probe + baseline telemetry (3 days).
- Week 1: bench matrix and recommended reserved throughput with a cost estimate.
- Decision checkpoint: go/no-go on chosen GPU variant and monthly reserved slab.

Attachments: pilot-sla-matrix.xlsx (blank template); auratek-example-workload.jsonl (sample requests).

Open questions for you
- Can you confirm whether the 512-token p95 target is for client-perceived time (first-response + streaming) or server token commit time?
- Do you have any hard constraints on model variants (open LLM vs closed) or disallowed quantization modes?

Next steps
- If that scope looks good, can Auratek confirm start on Mon Jul 31? We will assign a Dedicated engineer and book a 60-min bench kickoff.

Thanks,
Hannah

Thanks Hannah — fyi some quick technical framing before we kick off: 

Bench approach notes
- For streaming p95 we need to measure both first-byte and steady-state chunk latency. Streaming adds per-chunk overhead; aim for <12ms chunk overhead to meet 75ms p95 on 512 tokens (assuming 8 chunks average).
- KV cache behavior: if prefix reuse is >40% we can reduce effective compute by ~20–35% via cache hits; probe should capture reuse distribution.
- Concurrency isolation: run sets at 10/30/80 streams; measure tail latency and tail token throughput.

GPU trade-offs (initial opinion)
- H100: best headroom for p99 tail; good for heavy long-context models; higher cost.
- A100 80GB: solid balance for mixed short/long; well-understood quant stacks.
- L4 / 2:1 topologies: cost-effective for short-token, high-concurrency streaming but weaker for long context and kv cache heavy workloads.

Small ask for Auratek (to speed results)
- Can you include a 1% slice of true production traffic (anonymized) rather than synthetic to ensure prefix reuse fidelity?

I’ll draft the bench matrix and expected token/sec numbers and drop it into the shared Drive today.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Hannah / Karthik — thanks for the clear plan. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- The 75 ms p95 is client-perceived (time until the user sees the first usable token plus time to render streaming chunks). We are sensitive to UI jitter during streaming.
- We can provide a 1% anonymized traffic sample from production for the probe; SRE will export a redacted JSONL by Friday.
- No hard ban on quantization, but our ML team requires accuracy drift <0.5 BLEU (we test on the same eval set).
- Regarding GPUs, cost is a factor but we care most about predictable tail behavior — if H100 materially reduces p99 under the probe we can consider it.

We are comfortable with the start date of Mon Jul 31. Please send calendar invite for kickoff and include any pre-kickoff checklist.
